posts.text:
When Starlink became a lifeline for a family fighting to save their dad. ❤️

Nigel Norwood suffered cardiac arrest while camping at a remote beach in Western Australia, about 100 kilometres from the nearest hospital.

There was no mobile signal. His wife, Lynne, spotted another camper’s @Starlink and used it to call emergency services.

“This was the only way to get a call out from the campsite,” she later said.

While she called for help, their 16-year-old son performed CPR with another camper, and their 19-year-old son brought a nearby defibrillator. After three shocks, Nigel’s pulse returned. He received hospital care and recovered.

Starlink made that emergency call possible. When lives are at risk, a working connection can make all the difference.

This life-saving technology should be available in every part of the world.

SpaceX uses ARGON ION PROPULSION to move Starlink satellites through space 

And the engineering is pretty wild

Starlink satellites use argon Hall-effect thrusters  electric engines that ionize argon gas and accelerate the charged particles at extremely high speed

They allow Starlink satellites to:

• Raise themselves into operational orbit
• Maneuver around other spacecraft and debris
• Maintain their position in space
• Deorbit themselves at the end of their life

SpaceX originally used krypton, but switched its next-generation Starlink satellites to argon

The V2 Mini argon thruster produces:

• 170 mN of thrust
• 2.4X the thrust of the first-generation system
• 1.5X the specific impulse

And Starlink became the first spacecraft system to fly using argon propulsion in space

A Falcon 9 gets Starlink into space

Then these tiny electric engines keep thousands of satellites exactly where they need to be

posts.text: Grok @Bot can help with your taxes

quote.author: jasonfreedman
quote.name: Jason Freedman
quote.text:
I just gave my a Grokbot four years of past tax returns and financial files.  Just a dump of folders and unlabled files.

K-1s, 1099s, mortgage statements, HSA records, and every email with our CPA.  266 files.

I just said, please double check my CPA's work.

A few minutes later, it had found a lot of mistakes.

Mortgage interest left off our 2022 return entirely.

HSA payroll contributions counted twice, four years in a row, which created a penalty tax that never should have existed.

A missing IRA form for Jen that would have cost us.

On this year's return: home office errors, two K-1s missing, an outdated 1099, and startup losses we never claimed.

And a retirement contribution the return already deducted...that we hadn't actually deposited.  

I sent it all to our CPA.  They sent back an amended return.  The bot reviewed that too.

One fix went the wrong direction.  The explanation had typos.

Three versions later, all in one afternoon, it said ready to sign.

Just a few hours start to finish.  With about 90 seconds of my time and attention required. I was just the meat proxy hitting send as Grokbot watched the replies in my email.  

Our CPA is great and turned every fix around the same day.  

We chatted afterwards.  He wanted to know what I was using - just normal ole' grokbot.

I asked him what he was using?  No AI tools.  

I set him up with @magnetictax for next season (we're an investor).  All CPAs should be using Magnetic Tax or something like it.  Every single one.

All individuals should be double checking the work and past work with Grokbot or something like that.  

Want to copy the exact the prompt I used?  it was just this:

"Please do a thorough review of my taxes and help me understand if my CPA made any mistakes"

"Think deeply"

Or just tag your bot into this thread.

posts.author: elonmusk
posts.text:
Suggestion for you:

Pick an agent for work, and pick an agent for personal.

You could explore to do this all with Grok Bot (with many different types of bots)

Personally, I like @bot for work, and @Muse for personal agents.

It helps to create a clean separation for me.

Here are some reasons why Grok for Work:

- Grok is very good at coding, so if you want your bot to help you do engineering / building, Grok beats muse.

- Groks VM / Browser is very strong. I love it for deeper tasks that are work releated.

- Groks integration with X is goated. And I use X heavily for work.

Here are some reasons why @Muse for personal: 

- The simplicity with one agent who knows all is awesome

- The pricing is either free, or very cheap

- They have a history of keeping your private data safe

- They are focused on building personal agents, including training their models this way

- It gives me enough permissions to control my agents at the personal level 

- Building personal software within the app is so easy and well suited for personal use cases 

- Meta is all in on personal agents, which means significant resources being poured into product advancements (your agent gets better every day)

- Muse SDK allowing my agent to go with me on many devices is the right direction

- Meta's Sunglasses gets way more interesting once Muse is supported.
